requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation IS used to start a test behaviour on a test component and to wait until that test behaviour has terminated.
requirements.original: The call operation is used start a test behaviour on a test component and wait until that behaviour has terminated.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation has the syntax ObjectReference "." `call` "(" (FunctionInstance | AltstepInstance) ["," SimpleExpression] ")" ["->" [`value` Ref] [`verdict` Ref]] [`catch` "(" `timeout` ")" StatementBlock] [`catch` "(" `stop` ")" StatementBlock].
requirements.original:
ObjectReference "." call "(" ( FunctionInstance | AltstepInstance )
  ["," SimpleExpression ] ")"
  [ "->" [value Ref] [verdict Ref] ]
  [ catch "(" timeout ")" StatementBlock ]
  [ catch "(" stop ")" StatementBlock ]

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation IS blocking and implicitly uses a `start` operation on the test component.
requirements.original: Similar to the start operation on test components which is not blocking, the blocking call operation implicitly uses a start operation, but waits until either the started behaviour has terminated or some timeout has occurred.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The `call` operation SHALL wait until either the started test behaviour has terminated or the timeout duration has expired.
requirements.original: Similar to the start operation on test components which is not blocking, the blocking call operation implicitly uses a start operation, but waits until either the started behaviour has terminated or some timeout has occurred.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation MAY have a timeout duration in seconds, given as a SimpleExpression additional parameter.
requirements.original: A timeout duration in seconds can be given explicitly in the form of a SimpleExpression as an additional parameter to the call operation.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.condition: no timeout duration is given in the call operation
requirements.canonical: If no timeout duration is given, the `call` operation IS executed with an infinite timeout duration.
requirements.original: If no timeout duration is given, an infinite timeout duration is used.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The actions taken by the `call` operation depend on whether the execution of the started test behaviour is complete or incomplete.
requirements.original: The actions taken by the call operation are dependent on whether the execution of the started behaviour is complete or incomplete.

requirements.subject: ent:complete-execution
requirements.canonical: The execution of the started test behaviour IS complete when the started function terminates by executing a `return` statement or by reaching the end of its function body.
requirements.original: Complete execution occurs when the started function is terminated by executing a return statement or if it reaches the end of the function body.

readings: The execution of a called function is complete when it executes a `return` statement or reaches the end of its body; the execution of a called altstep is complete when the altstep terminates normally after executing one of its alternatives.
Only called functions can have a complete execution; a called altstep execution is always incomplete.
ambiguity.issue: The rule only mentions functions although the call operation also accepts altstep instances (see the example a_myFourthBehaviour); the first reading is chosen as altsteps are explicitly allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:incomplete-execution
requirements.canonical: If the started test behaviour terminates for any reason other than executing a `return` statement or reaching the end of its function body, the execution IS incomplete.
requirements.original: If the started behaviour is terminated for any other reason, the execution is incomplete.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-stop-clause
requirements.condition: the called component was stopped or killed and a catch stop clause is added to the call operation
requirements.canonical: If the execution is incomplete because the called component was stopped or killed and a `catch(stop)` clause is present, the StatementBlock of the `catch(stop)` clause SHALL be executed before the `call` operation terminates.
requirements.original: If the incomplete execution occurs because the called component was stopped or killed and a catch stop clause is added to the call operation, the StatementBlock of that clause is executed before the call operation terminates.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.condition: the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timeout clause is present
requirements.canonical: If the started test behaviour does not terminate within the given timeout duration and a `catch(timeout)` clause is present, the called component SHALL be implicitly stopped.
requirements.original: If the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timout clause is added to the call operation, the called component is implicitly stopped and the StatementBlock of the catch timeout clause is executed before the call operation terminates.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-timeout-clause
requirements.condition: the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timeout clause is present
requirements.canonical: If the started test behaviour does not terminate within the given timeout duration and a `catch(timeout)` clause is present, the StatementBlock of the `catch(timeout)` clause SHALL be executed before the `call` operation terminates.
requirements.original: If the started behaviour does not terminate in the given timeout duration and a catch timout clause is added to the call operation, the called component is implicitly stopped and the StatementBlock of the catch timeout clause is executed before the call operation terminates.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.condition: execution is incomplete and not handled by a catch clause
requirements.canonical: If the execution is incomplete and no matching `catch(stop)` or `catch(timeout)` clause handles it, the `call` operation SHALL end with a test case error.
requirements.original: In all other cases when the execution is incomplete, the call operation ends with a test case error.

requirements.canonical: The `create` operation SHALL NOT be used with the `any component` or `all component` keywords.
requirements.original: Operation: create

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `start` operation SHALL NOT be used with the `any component` or `all component` keywords.
requirements.original: Operation: start

requirements.original: Operation: running; Allowed: Yes but from MTC only; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: any component.running; all component.running;; Comment: Is there any PTC performing test behaviour? Are all PTCs performing test behaviour?

requirements.canonical: `any component.running` and `all component.running` SHALL NOT be used in a test component other than the MTC.
requirements.original: Operation: running; Allowed: Yes but from MTC only; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: any component.running; all component.running;; Comment: Is there any PTC performing test behaviour? Are all PTCs performing test behaviour?

requirements.subject: ent:any-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: `any component.done` and `all component.done` SHALL NOT be used in a test component other than the MTC.
requirements.original: Operation: done; Allowed: Yes but from MTC only; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: any component.done; all component.done;; Comment: Is there any PTC that completed execution? Did all PTCs complete their execution?

requirements.subject: ent:done-operation
requirements.canonical: `any component.done` IS true if any PTC has completed its execution.
requirements.original: Operation: done; Allowed: Yes but from MTC only; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: any component.done; all component.done;; Comment: Is there any PTC that completed execution? Did all PTCs complete their execution?

requirements.canonical: `all component.done` IS true if all PTCs have completed their execution.
requirements.original: Operation: done; Allowed: Yes but from MTC only; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: any component.done; all component.done;; Comment: Is there any PTC that completed execution? Did all PTCs complete their execution?

requirements.subject: ent:any-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: `any component.killed` and `all component.killed` MAY be used in the MTC.
requirements.original: Operation: killed; Allowed: Yes but from MTC only; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: any component.killed; all component.killed;; Comment: Is there any PTC that ceased to exist? Did all PTCs cease to exist?

requirements.subject: ent:any-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: `any component.killed` and `all component.killed` SHALL NOT be used in a test component other than the MTC.
requirements.original: Operation: killed; Allowed: Yes but from MTC only; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: any component.killed; all component.killed;; Comment: Is there any PTC that ceased to exist? Did all PTCs cease to exist?

requirements.canonical: `any component.killed` IS true if any PTC has ceased to exist.
requirements.original: Operation: killed; Allowed: Yes but from MTC only; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: any component.killed; all component.killed;; Comment: Is there any PTC that ceased to exist? Did all PTCs cease to exist?

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: `all component.stop` MAY be used in the MTC.
requirements.original: Operation: stop; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: all component.stop;; Comment: Stop the behaviour on all PTCs.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: `all component.stop` SHALL NOT be used in a test component other than the MTC.
requirements.original: Operation: stop; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: all component.stop;; Comment: Stop the behaviour on all PTCs.

requirements.subject: ent:any-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `stop` operation SHALL NOT be used with the `any component` keyword.
requirements.original: Operation: stop; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: all component.stop;; Comment: Stop the behaviour on all PTCs.

requirements.subject: ent:stop-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `all component.stop` operation SHALL stop the behaviour on all PTCs.
requirements.original: Operation: stop; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: all component.stop;; Comment: Stop the behaviour on all PTCs.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: `all component.kill` MAY be used in the MTC.
requirements.original: Operation: kill; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: all component.kill;; Comment: Kill all PTCs, i.e. they cease to exist.

requirements.subject: ent:all-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: `all component.kill` SHALL NOT be used in a test component other than the MTC.
requirements.original: Operation: kill; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: all component.kill;; Comment: Kill all PTCs, i.e. they cease to exist.

requirements.subject: ent:any-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `kill` operation SHALL NOT be used with the `any component` keyword.
requirements.original: Operation: kill; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: all component.kill;; Comment: Kill all PTCs, i.e. they cease to exist.

requirements.subject: ent:kill-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The `all component.kill` operation SHALL kill all PTCs, so that they cease to exist.
requirements.original: Operation: kill; Col3: Yes but from MTC only; Example: all component.kill;; Comment: Kill all PTCs, i.e. they cease to exist.

requirements.subject: ent:any-component-keyword
requirements.canonical: The `any component` and `all component` keywords refer to PTCs only and do not consider the MTC.
requirements.original: NOTE: any and all refer to PTCs only, i.e. the MTC is not considered.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.condition: the execution of the started behaviour is complete
requirements.canonical: After complete execution of the started test behaviour, the `out` and `inout` actual parameters of the called function or altstep instance SHALL be updated in the same manner as in a normal function or altstep invocation.
requirements.original: After complete execution of the started behaviour, the out and inout actual parameters given to the actual parameter list of the called function or altstep instance will be updated in the same manner as if it was a normal function/altstep invocation.

requirements.subject: ent:value-clause
requirements.condition: the called function has a return clause
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation MAY have a redirect clause with a `value` clause that assigns the return value of the called function to a variable, if the called function has a return clause.
requirements.original: Additionally, a redirect clause can be added to the operation which allows assignment of the return result (in case that the called function has a return clause) to a variable via the value clause and also the assignment of the termination verdict of the called component via the verdict clause.

requirements.subject: ent:verdict-clause
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation MAY have a redirect clause with a `verdict` clause that assigns the termination verdict of the called component to a variable.
requirements.original: Additionally, a redirect clause can be added to the operation which allows assignment of the return result (in case that the called function has a return clause) to a variable via the value clause and also the assignment of the termination verdict of the called component via the verdict clause.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.condition: the execution of the started behaviour is incomplete
requirements.canonical: In all cases of incomplete execution, the variables referenced in the `value` and `verdict` clauses and in `out` and `inout` actual parameters SHALL stay unchanged and no assignment SHALL be made.
requirements.original: In all cases of incomplete execution, the variables referenced in the value and verdict clause or in out and inout actual parameters will stay unchanged and no assignment will be made.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.condition: the called component is non-alive and has already been started or called, or it has been killed
requirements.canonical: A `call` operation SHALL NOT be applied to a test component that is not created alive and has already been started or called once, nor to a test component that has been killed.
requirements.original: If the called component is not created alive and has already been started or called once or if it has been killed, additional call operations are not allowed.

readings: A call operation is not allowed on a killed test component (alive or not) and on a non-alive test component that has already been started or called once.
A call operation is not allowed on a non-alive test component that has already been started, called or killed; the killed condition only applies to non-alive components.
ambiguity.issue: The scope of 'or if it has been killed' is unclear; the first reading is chosen since a killed component of any kind cannot execute behaviour. The text also does not say whether violation is a compile-time or runtime error; the example shows it is a test case error.

requirements.subject: ent:object-reference
requirements.canonical: The ObjectReference of a `call` operation SHALL be of a component type.
requirements.original: a) The ObjectReference shall be of a component type.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The function or altstep invoked in a `call` operation SHALL have a `runs on` clause referencing a component type to which the called component is compatible.
requirements.original: b) The function or altstep invoked in a call test component operation shall have a runs `on definition` referencing a component type to which the called component is compatible (see clause 6.3.2.7).

ambiguity.issue: 'runs on definition' is used instead of the usual 'runs on clause', and 'call test component operation' instead of 'call operation'.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter
requirements.canonical: Every formal parameter of the function or altstep invoked in a `call` operation SHALL be of a component data type.
requirements.original: c) All formal parameters of the function or altstep invoked in a call test component operation shall be of a component data type.

requirements.subject: ent:call-operation
requirements.canonical: The return type of the function invoked in a `call` operation SHALL be a component data type.
requirements.original: d) The return value of the function invoked from a call test component operation shall be of a component data type.

ambiguity.issue: The restriction concerns the return type, but 'return value' is used.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-duration
requirements.canonical: The optional SimpleExpression giving the timeout duration of a `call` operation SHALL be of type `float`.
requirements.original: e) The optional SimpleExpression representing the timer value shall be of a float type.

ambiguity.issue: The semantic description calls it 'timeout duration', the restriction 'timer value' although no timer is involved.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-timeout-clause
requirements.canonical: A `catch(timeout)` clause SHALL NOT be present in a `call` operation unless a timeout duration is given.
requirements.original: f) The optional catch `timeout clause may be present only if the timeout value has been defined.`

ambiguity.issue: 'timeout value' is used instead of 'timeout duration'.

requirements.subject: ent:value-clause
requirements.canonical: The variable in the `value` clause of a `call` operation SHALL be compatible with the return type of the invoked function.
requirements.original: g) The variable in the value clause shall be compatible with the return value of the invoked function.

ambiguity.issue: Compatibility is a property of types; 'return value' is used where the return type is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:verdict-clause
requirements.canonical: The variable in the `verdict` clause of a `call` operation SHALL be of type `verdicttype`.
requirements.original: h) The variable in the verdict clause shall be of type verdicttype.
